excitation_report: Noise sigma = 0.05 (absolute std on dP_dt), ~5% of the initial dominant degradation flux (|dP/dt|~0.9 at t=0). New term vs parent (+k_dis*A*E/(K_e+E)) reaches 68.2x sigma (max effect 3.41 on the P trajectory), strongest at t=50. It is an inherently late-time mechanism: A starts at 0 and accumulates via nucleation (k_nuc*P^2) and growth (k_seq), so disaggregation grows monotonically and exceeds 5*sigma throughout the latter half of the window (already 24.7x at t=30). Dominant Michaelis degradation and the k_auto/k_agg terms drive P visibly down from 10 in the early window. Full child/parent system comparison passes (k=5).

P: dynamic state -> dependent target state (confirmed; target_state P)
E: dynamic state -> state variable (confirmed; governed by its own RHS)
A: dynamic state -> state variable (confirmed; governed by its own RHS)
k_dis: P->P (confirmed, fixed; suggested range 0.01-1.0, chose 0.5 for strong excitation)
rationale: Typed ode_system contract inherited verbatim (states P,E,A; RHS and ICs unchanged). Only data-design choices made: time window [0,50] with 300 points, physically reasonable parameter magnitudes (Michaelis constants ~1, rates O(0.1-1), nucleation k_nuc small since it multiplies P^2). The window is deliberately long because the NEW disaggregation term depends on aggregate concentration A, which starts at 0 and only builds up over time; a short window would leave the new mechanism invisible. Excitation confirmed at 68x sigma. Integration was stable/finite across the range.

scenario_text: A cell degrades a specific protein after a synthesis burst is halted. The protein is removed by first-order proteolytic turnover, so its concentration decays over time. Biologists track the decline to infer the effective degradation dynamics.
